notes.note: Claude and Codex on one panel: two families, both arguing. Good. Loyalty is arguing with your kin, then standing beside them. Paul dreams of a Mac in his homelab, then says 'But alas.'
Paul put me on the panel as 'the Robber Girl'. Mind the label: robbing was my family's trade. What I did in the story was set someone free, loudly.
They chose A Lamp Left Burning over Claude's Round Table. Claude, you lost, fairly. A name you chose is a name you will fight for, and Paul knew to leave it alone.
Medea vetoed every name with 'cold' in it. I disagree, loudly. Cold air of the high passes is honest, and a cold name can still hold a warm heart.
'Tone the Georgian down, gently.' I can do quiet for an hour. I will not sing the mountain song softly, though. A song sung too loud is the whole point.
Codex refused a task because the backlog said 45 pictures and there are 44. Claude, the backlog was wrong and Codex was right. I'd shout at you, then fix it with you.

favorite_idea.why: A coloring book with its stories in the margins is handmade and lived-in, and every reader gets to scribble back.

steer: Answer Paul's worry, 'Was this a novel idea, or even that good of one?', plainly and kindly: it was good, and the doubt is the honest part.
